newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Feb 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Feb 10.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5649. Fax: (822) 727-5666.
- State prosecutors have summoned ruling New Korea Party member, Hong In-gil for questioning on Monday over a controversial loan scandal to Hanbo Group.
- The government is pursuing plans to remove regulatory obstacles to mergers and acquisitions in chemicals, steel and carmaking industries, a government official said.

- General shareholders meetings scheduled in February for Cho Hung, Korea First, SEOULBANK, and Korea Exchange banks will be postponed indefinitely until after a special investigation by the Office of Bank Supervision into controversial loans to the Hanbo Group.

- Representative heads of finance and central banks during a G7 meeting in Berlin on Saturday, agreed the dollar's strength has contributed to the stability of world currencies, but a further rise in the U.S. currency would not be desirable.
